correctness.rationale: The precise power-sum polynomial coefficient bound gives H_s(x)-x/c^s in pZ_p<x>, for s=1,2. This establishes a global restricted analytic interpolation F(x)=x(x-1)/(2c^2)+pR(x). Its derivative has a unique p-adic zero by strict contraction, and its normalized Taylor series has a convergent square root producing a global bijective isometry. This proves the entire translated-square image, fiber root counts, exact period and Haar measure. Nine full finite-modulus enumerations (2087 indices) corroborate but are not substituted for the proof.

Distinct ordinary harmonic work and arithmetic-progression integrality abstracts do not establish the image classification. A general analytic Morse method is acknowledged; applying it globally here requires a new explicit restricted-series coefficient estimate for this arithmetic family. Search does not establish priority, and residual risks are reported.

value.rationale: The second elementary symmetric reciprocal progression is an established natural arithmetic object. Determining all attainable p^k residues at the primes dividing the step, rather than only integrality, is a motivated gap. The universal translated-square image, explicit fiber spectrum, and density p/(2(p+1)) classify every local representation, with genuinely infinite scope. The new arithmetic interpolation and uniform perturbation verification are essential; this is not a bare restatement of the standard Morse lemma.
